issues.situation: On the benchmark's large terrain objectives (homes/NMLs are 7"x11.5" ruins; obj_center is two trapezoids covering x 16.2-27.8", y 25-35"), the usual trigger is a partial foothold. In 5 of 6 V9 sweep triggers only part of the unit was in range: s7454 Beta 1/3, s7462 Orks Gretchin 1/10 plus a Battlewagon, s7469 Lootas 3/4, s7474 Lootas 6/9. HOLD executes as REMAIN_STATIONARY (AIDecisionMaker.gd ~7031), so with the fix the holder keeps most of its OC off the objective. Because the need never drops, every second holder is also pinned in place: at s7462 the Battlewagon is pinned where the base freed it. Pass 2 then pulls another unit to supply OC the holder could add by stepping its other models in. This pull cascades: at s7454 Alpha takes the centre and Gamma inherits a 3-turn, ~27" walk to home_2, and a horizon-1 rollout cannot see its round-5 cost. This is not shown to be worse than base, which never flipped the objective, but it is a costly way to fill the need.
issues.proposed_change: Benchmark a variant alongside the fix rather than replacing it. Under FIX_LONE_FLIP, when the holder has alive models outside range that can reach the objective this move, give it a 'move' assignment toward the objective (the existing move executor, _compute_movement_toward_target). Credit oc_consumed with the OC of those models (at most unit_oc minus its in-range OC), and let pass 2 pull other units only for the rest. Note this variant changes the s7454 outcome: Gamma would again lone-flip obj_nml_1. So it needs its own value check.

issues.situation: Pass 2.5 (attack conversion) double-reopens a converted holder. With the fix, the holder's oc_consumed is 0 and the need N stays open. Then reopened = max(0, T - (F - U) + 1) is added on top, so the need after conversion is about N + T - F + U + 1. With the s7454 numbers (N 4, F 5, E 8, U 9) that gives 17 against base 13; the correct value is 7 (Beta's 3 in-range OC leaving). Backfill can then pull an extra unit. This is rare: none of the 21 trigger holds in the local replay logs was followed by a reopen on the same objective.
issues.proposed_change: In the pass-2.5 hold branch, when FIX_LONE_FLIP zeroed the holder's consumption, reopen only the holder's in-range OC at that objective (_unit_oc_at_position), not the max(..., h_threat - h_left + 1) formula.

issues.situation: The fix also covers enemy_strong objectives. By definition there, enemy_oc is at least the OC we can bring within two moves. With FIX_FAR_TRIP and FIX_OVERCOMMIT off, nothing limits how many units the now-larger ledger sends: the base's leftover need (N minus the holder's OC) usually drew one unit, while the full N can draw two or three into a fight the planner already rates as lost. This is low frequency: all 21 trigger holds in the replay logs were enemy_weak or contested, as was the s7454 centre.
issues.proposed_change: Limit zero consumption to enemy_weak and contested, which is all the evidence covers, and keep base consumption on enemy_strong. Alternatively, cap the reopened need at what pass 2 can reach this turn.

issues.situation: test_holder_on_our_objective_still_covers_it passes no matter what the hold pass does. With enemy OC 2 against ours 3 and no enemy one move away, the objective is held_threatened and its need is 0 before any hold. So it does not check that held states still consume. There are no tests for two partial holders (the pinning change), a contested tie, or the attack-conversion reopen.
issues.proposed_change: Add a held_threatened case with an enemy unit one move away (a positive projected need that the holder still covers), a tie case (state contested, so one more unit is sent), and a two-foothold case that asserts both hold.

issues.situation: The validation is thinner than the report implies. The fix's real s7454 plan (Alpha to the centre, Gamma to home_2) differs from the measured alternative (Gamma advances to the centre), and it was only replayed with the fix in both seats; P1's own LONE_FLIP fired at obj_center (5 vs 14) in the same replay. That covers 2 to 6 seeds, not a 36-seed forced branch. The downstream changes at the s7431 and s7455 fires were not inspected. The related s7455 r1 P2 finding (+4.30) is not addressed, and cannot be: the trigger never occurs in round 1 (0 of 61 V9 round-1 movement saves).
issues.proposed_change: Before the benchmark, run the 36-seed forced-branch check of the fix's actual two-unit plan with FIX_LONE_FLIP on in P2's seat only, preferably with a 2-round horizon so Gamma's walk home is costed. Describe s7455 r1 as out of scope.

issues.situation: The benchmark harness keeps no logs for completed games (the round-3 bench results show "logs":0 and every fire tag reads [0,0]), so a '[LONE_FLIP]' fire count will read 0 even when the fix fires. A related gap: _unit_alive_oc ignores battle-shock, so a battle-shocked holder (0 in-range OC) on an uncontrolled objective still zeroes its need of 1. This is the same double count, but outside the fix's state list.
issues.proposed_change: Judge firing by the share of non-identical pairs, or turn on log retention for completed games in the bench run. Optionally also apply zero consumption when the holder's in-range OC is 0, whatever the objective's state.

reviews.fires_in_bench: It fires often enough to move the benchmark, unlike V9's keeper fix. Evidence: (1) V9 round-4 sweep movement saves (same crucible_of_battle deployment, 11e terrain-hosted objectives): the trigger appears in 0 of 61 round-1 saves, 1 of 21 round-2 and 5 of 26 round-3 (3 of 9 among round-3 saves taken before any unit moved). It appeared in all four matchup directions. In 5 of the 6 triggers the base's hold had zeroed the need, so the fix reopens the objective; 5 of the 6 were on obj_center. (2) Local replay logs with FIX_HELD_DUP on (V6–V9 code): 7 of 70 movement plans (round 1 0/9, round 2 3/26, round 3 3/24, round 4 1/11). (3) Every benchmark objective is hosted on a large ruin: 7"x11.5" for homes and NMLs, about 11.6"x10" for the centre. Units can therefore hold part of an objective the enemy also stands on without being engaged, from round 3 on. Estimate: about 0.5 to 1 fire per game per candidate seat (rounds 2-5, mostly obj_center in rounds 3-5) and about 0.25 to 0.5 changed plans per game. So roughly 25-40% of candidate games, and about half of the side-swapped pairs, will be non-identical, in all three fixtures. Orks games may fire somewhat more often, because large mobs can clip the zone with one model (Gretchin 1/10 at s7462). Caveat: the harness keeps no logs for completed games, so '[LONE_FLIP]' tag counts will read 0; count non-identical pairs instead.
reviews.strengths: The root cause is correct and verified in code. oc_needed (= enemy_oc - friendly_oc + 1) already includes the holder's in-range OC, and HOLD executes as REMAIN_STATIONARY, yet the hold pass subtracted the whole alive unit OC again, including out-of-range models and battle-shocked units. The offline position check reproduces s7454 exactly: Beta with 1 of 3 models on the centre, 5 vs 8, need 4, unit OC 9, so the need was zeroed. The change is one condition, gated by FIX_LONE_FLIP, and setting the param to 0 restores the base exactly. It adds no new veto: an objective where we hold a foothold is now treated like the same objective without one, by the existing tuned scoring. That fits the 'no broad trip/race veto' lesson, and it pushes units toward contested primary objectives rather than holding them back (the FAR_TRIP failure mode). Held states are deliberately left alone, which fits the round-3 REINFORCE-CAP lesson. It reverses the s7454 failure, and the guardrail decisions stay unchanged. At s7431 r3 the reopened home_2 cannot outscore Beta's centre move (centre priority 20.0 vs home_2 12.2). At s7441, pinning Logan on the centre matches a measured-neutral alternative (E 0.00). Its trigger is common enough in the benchmark to show an effect.
reviews.summary: Verdict: ok, no major issue. The double count is real: under HOLD (= REMAIN_STATIONARY) a holder on an enemy-held or tied objective adds nothing beyond the in-range OC that friendly_oc already counts, but the base subtracted its whole unit OC. The narrow fix stops that and leaves held states alone. Under the game-impact lens I found no concrete, common situation where it makes full-game play worse than base. Its effects all run through the existing ledger: pass 2 may send units to the reopened objective, extra footholds are pinned in place, the attack-conversion reopen, and DIM-RETURNS. These make foothold objectives behave like the same objective without a foothold. Six minor points: (1) on the benchmark's large terrain objectives, partial footholds are the usual trigger, and the fix fills the need by pulling and pinning other units rather than stepping the holder's own models in, which can cascade (s7454: Gamma inherits a 3-turn walk home); (2) the attack conversion double-reopens (4+13=17 vs a correct 7; rare); (3) including enemy_strong can stack units into fights rated lost (not seen in the logs); (4) the held-state test passes trivially; (5) the validation was fix-in-both-seats with 2-6 seeds, the s7454 outcome differs from the measured alternative, and s7455 r1 is not addressed; (6) the bench harness keeps no logs, so fire-tag counts will read 0. Frequency: about 0.5-1 fire per game per seat, mostly on obj_center in rounds 3-5, so roughly half of benchmark pairs will diverge. Offline evidence scripts: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-warhammer-40k-godot/72451711-ff9e-5f4b-a27c-d739a3534701/scratchpad/lf_narrow_review/pos_trigger.py (approximates objective states and the trigger from saves) and /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-warhammer-40k-godot/72451711-ff9e-5f4b-a27c-d739a3534701/scratchpad/lf_narrow_review/scan_holds.py (counts trigger holds in replay logs). These offline checks approximate the engine's range test and were not validated by running Godot. Housekeeping: I also wrote /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-warhammer-40k-godot/72451711-ff9e-5f4b-a27c-d739a3534701/scratchpad/base_ai.gd. It is byte-identical to the 5e70bc2 AIDecisionMaker.gd (same md5 as git show); if an earlier file with that name existed, it was overwritten.

issues.situation: COORD-4 pass 2.5 in _assign_units_to_objectives, which runs after pass 2, still assumes a hold used up its share of the need. When _melee_chase_gate turns a HOLD into an ATTACK, the pass computes reopened = maxi(oc_consumed, h_threat - (friendly_oc - unit_oc) + 1) and ADDS it to obj_oc_remaining[a_oid]. That formula sizes the whole shortfall once the holder leaves. In base the hold had already taken the need down (usually to 0), so the result came out at about that shortfall. With LONE-FLIP, oc_consumed is 0 and the need R stays in the ledger, and pass 2 has already sent OC to cover R. The objective therefore ends up needing R + X instead of about X. With the finding's numbers (need 4; holder unit OC 9 with 3 of it in range; friendly 5; enemy 8): base re-opens to max(4, 13) = 13. The fix re-opens to 4 (or whatever pass 2 already covered) + 13 = 17. The real need after the holder leaves is 8 - 2 + 1 = 7. The backfill loop, including OBJ-BACKFILL-1 switches, then sends one or two extra units there. This path is reachable in the benchmark. The fixture Custodian Guard (5 models, OC2, M6, ranged spear S4 A2, unlike the custodes_lions S5 lists of the sweep games) count as melee seekers under _is_melee_focused_unit, and so do Ork Stormboyz, Gretchin and Mek. Custodes aggression is 1.5, so a holder leaves for an enemy within 12-14". The only exception is when both centroids are within 3.79" of the marker, which is uncommon on the 7x11.5" and 2x(11.5x8)" hosting areas. The report's claim 'every other pass untouched' is therefore wrong.
issues.proposed_change: In the new branch, mark the hold (e.g. assignments[uid]["lone_flip_hold"] = true). In pass 2.5, when lone_flip_on is set and the converted hold has that mark, re-open only the OC that actually leaves: reopened = _unit_oc_at_position(a.objective_pos, uid, a_unit, snapshot.get("units", {}), hd_obj_by_id.get(a_oid, {}), hd_mm), the holder's in-range OC, instead of maxi(oc_consumed, h_threat - h_left + 1). Keep the base formula when the param is 0. Add a test with a melee-only partial holder (1 model in range) on an enemy-held objective, an enemy about 6" away and two free units. Assert that the holder converts to ATTACK, that the [COORD-4] re-open equals its in-range OC, and that the second free unit is not also sent there.

issues.situation: The test assertion is tangled with pass-3 screening. _goes_to() only checks objective_id == obj_x and action move/advance, and a pass-3 support move passes that check too. The 150-pt 'free' unit has no weapons, so it is a screening candidate (points <= SCREEN_CHEAP_UNIT_POINTS*1.5, no ranged weapon), and pass 3 at Competitive difficulty gives it SCREEN-PROTECT. Without that, _find_best_remaining_objective would send it toward obj_x with action 'move'. Test 1 would then pass on base, and test 2 ('not stacked on an objective we already control') would fail with the fix. Today the base failure has the right root cause (pass 2 saw a need of 0), but it depends on this side effect.
issues.proposed_change: Assert on the pass instead: plan.free.assign_pass == "capture" with objective obj_x in test 1, and not a capture of obj_x in tests 2 and 3. Alternatively, give 'free' a ranged weapon or 200 pts so pass 3 cannot screen it. Optionally also assert the holder's oc_consumed == 0 when the fix is on.

issues.situation: Test 2 does not show that held objectives are left out of the gate. With the holder at 3 vs enemy 2 (held_threatened), the need before the hold is 0, so base consumption and LONE-FLIP's zero consumption leave the same ledger. The test would still pass if the gate also covered held_safe/held_threatened. No test covers the 'contested' (equal OC) state, or the new behaviour that a second holder on an enemy-held or tied objective is no longer freed.
issues.proposed_change: In test 2, place an enemy unit one move outside range so the held_threatened need is > 0 and the base hold covers it, then assert the free unit is not captured there. Add a contested case (equal OC) where the free unit is sent. Add a two-holder enemy-held case asserting that both hold.

issues.situation: Several statements in narrow.json do not match the code or the data. (1) 'every other pass untouched' is wrong: pass 2.5 reads oc_consumed, and holds on enemy-held or tied objectives are never freed now because the need never drops. A second holder that base freed once the first had 'covered' the need now stays, and that behaviour change is not mentioned. (2) Guardrail s7452 r2, the 6th listed, is not checked. In its save obj_center is held by P1, so the fix should not fire, but this was not replayed. (3) At the finding the fix outcome ran the fix in both seats (P1 fired too), only seeds 5001/5002 are paired with base A, and the 6-seed fix mean of -1.2 has no matching base mean. (4) The report says '3 of 5 fires on our own home', but the listed fires are 2 on our own home (s7431, s7455 r3), 1 on the enemy home (s7455 r2, P1) and 2 on the centre.
issues.proposed_change: Correct the claims and replay s7452 r2. At the finding, report a single-seat comparison (fix for P2 only), paired with A on the same seeds.

issues.situation: A battle-shocked holder has 0 OC in friendly_oc (_unit_oc_at_position returns 0), but already_on_obj still marks it as a holder and it stays put. Base subtracted its unit OC, which roughly anticipates its recovery at its next Command phase. LONE-FLIP subtracts nothing, so pass 2 may send an extra unit to cover OC that will come back.
issues.proposed_change: Keep the base consumption for battle-shocked holders in the LONE-FLIP branch (e.g. add `and not unit.flags.battle_shocked` to the condition), or record the choice in the comment.

issues.situation: Scope notes, not defects. The same double count still exists on held_threatened objectives (the projected need minus the holder's whole OC); it is deliberately left, but this is not stated. A partial holder is kept REMAIN_STATIONARY although moving its out-of-range models in would add OC (Beta's two trailing models are OC 6 at the finding). The related s7455 r1 Prosecutor finding is not touched: the centre was uncontrolled with no holder, so the fix cannot fire there.
issues.proposed_change: State these limits in the const comment and the report. A 'tighten onto the objective' move for partial holders could follow later as a separate param.

reviews.fires_in_bench: The LONE-FLIP branch never fires in round 1. From round 2 it fires in any movement plan where a unit that is not engaged and has not yet moved has a model on an objective the enemy controls or ties (hosting-area overlap, marker within 3.79", or centroid). For those states the need is at least 1, so that unit always gets HOLD. I did not run Godot. I statically checked 108 V9 movement-decision saves from the round-4 sweeps in the same three matchups (rounds 1-3 only, positions picked by the critic so biased, on the sweep Custodes and Ork lists rather than the fixture lists). Results: 0/61 positions in round 1, 1/21 in round 2 and 6/26 in round 3 had such a holder. In 5 of the 7, the holder's unit OC was at least the need, meaning base cut the need to 0 and the fix re-opens it for pass 2. The designer reports 5 fires in 6 one-round replays. Estimate: about 1-2 fires per side per full game, mostly in rounds 3-5, with the plan changing in about half of them, so most paired benchmark games will diverge (unlike V9's 64/64 identical pairs). The double re-open path (major issue) is likely common in the benchmark too: the fixtures' 5-model S4-spear Custodian Guard and the Ork Stormboyz/Gretchin/Mek are melee seekers, so many LONE-FLIP holds will be converted to ATTACK in pass 2.5. Custodes aggression is 1.5, which sets the hold-chase limit to 12-14".
reviews.strengths: The diagnosis is right and checked in code. For enemy_weak, enemy_strong and contested objectives the need is enemy_oc - friendly_oc + 1, and the projected extra also subtracts friendly_oc. friendly_oc already contains the holder's in-range OC, and a HOLD runs as REMAIN_STATIONARY, so subtracting the holder's whole unit OC again is a real double count; at the finding it cut obj_center's need from 4 to 0. The change is as small as it can be: one gated branch in the hold pass. FIX_LONE_FLIP=0 restores base behaviour exactly; the only difference is an extra parameters_used entry in decision records. get_param is read once outside the loop, so there is no hot-loop cost. No debug log is removed and a clear [LONE_FLIP] line is added. Style matches the FIX_* conventions, and the patch applies cleanly to 5e70bc2. Side benefit: a second holder on a tied objective is no longer freed after the first one 'covers' a need of 1. The test drives the real _evaluate_all_objectives and _assign_units_to_objectives path, pins the override and then erases it, and fails on base at the intended assertion. The fix fires in benchmark-like positions from round 2, so the benchmark can measure it. The report is candid about risks and measurement limits.
reviews.summary: Verdict: revise. The double count the cluster describes is real, and the hold-pass fix is correct and minimal. But the patch changes what a hold's oc_consumed means without updating the code that reads it. COORD-4 pass 2.5 adds a converted holder's full shortfall on top of a need that LONE-FLIP left unconsumed, and that pass 2 has usually already covered. Any objective whose melee-seeker holder leaves to attack gets over-committed: a need of 17 instead of the true 7 at the finding's numbers, which means one or two extra backfilled units. This path is not rare in the benchmark: the fixtures' 5-model S4-spear Custodian Guard and Ork Stormboyz/Gretchin/Mek are melee seekers, unlike the custodes_lions lists in the sweep games where the finding was measured. Concrete change: for LONE-FLIP holds, re-open only the holder's in-range OC, and add a test for it. The tests should also assert on assign_pass. Today they pass or fail partly because pass 3 screens the 150-pt weaponless test unit, and the held-state case does not tell the gated and ungated versions apart. The report's 'every other pass untouched' claim, its missing s7452 r2 guardrail and its fix-in-both-seats measurement should be corrected. I estimate the fix fires 1-2 times per side per game from round 3 on, so most benchmark pairs will diverge.

issues.situation: Co-holder pinning, a side effect missing from the design's risks and tests. On a non-held objective, holders no longer reduce `obj_oc_remaining`, so remaining stays > 0 and every later pass-1 holder takes `should_hold` (REMAIN_STATIONARY). Base kept only the holders needed to cover the need plus the keeper and freed the rest. The only V9 benchmark-layout game in the local logs (session_20261030_163127 / _163636, Custodes mirror) shows this twice in one phase. At r4 P1, P2 had moved onto obj_nml_2 and the centre was contested. Allarus #2 ("keeping hold — the other unit(s) here are freed", oc_consumed 3 = its unit OC = the need) freed Blade Champions A and B. Prosecutors (consumed 3 of 8) freed at least one centre co-holder. The freed units walked back toward P1's home to charge P2's raiders. Under the patch they would stand still on the two contested objectives, and pass 2 would add another unit to each. On take_and_hold_mirror_1 the hosting areas are 7"x11.5" (centre about 11.5"x10"). A squad passing by with one model clipping an area therefore becomes a co-holder and stays pinned for as long as the objective stays contested. The sign of this change is unproven: keeping holders on a close fight is usually right.
issues.proposed_change: Keep the corrected ledger, but give co-holders a consistent exit. In pass 1, a non-keeper co-holder on a non-held objective may leave when its best other candidate outscores its hold candidate. When it leaves, add its in-range OC (`_unit_oc_at_position` with the FIX-HELD-DUP objective) back to `obj_oc_remaining[oid]`, so pass 2 can backfill it. Add a two-holder contested-objective case to test_ai_fix_lone_flip.gd. Have [LONE_FLIP] print how many co-holders it kept, so benchmark diffs can attribute changes to pinning versus re-opened need.

issues.situation: Pass 2.5 re-open counts the need twice for LONE_FLIP holds. When a pass-1 holder on a non-held objective (oc_consumed now 0) is converted to ATTACK by `_melee_chase_gate`, COORD-4 adds `max(0, threat - (friendly_oc - unit_oc) + 1)` on top of a need that was never reduced. This can happen when the holder's centroid is over 3.79" from the marker (common with the large areas) and an enemy is within 10". Example from the V9 benchmark game, r3 P1 centre: enemy 20 vs friendly 16, need 5; a 10-OC Custodian Guard holder was converted. Base re-opened 15 and backfilled two squads. The patch gives 5 + 15 = 20; the correct figure is 5 plus the holder's in-range OC. The COORD-4 backfill / OBJ-BACKFILL-1 then pulls one more unit, possibly off a lower-scored capture. In V9-era logs this co-occurs in only about 7% of firing phases.
issues.proposed_change: In pass 2.5, when the hold's oc_consumed is 0 because FIX_LONE_FLIP applied (non-held objective, need > 0), set `reopened` to the holder's in-range OC at that objective (the OC that actually leaves) instead of `h_threat - h_left + 1`. Store a flag such as `assignments[uid]["lone_flip_hold"] = true` in pass 1 so pass 2.5 can tell these holds apart.

issues.situation: The partial holder still stands still, so a second unit fills the need it could fill itself. The benchmark armies differ from the 3-model sweep lists: they field 5-model Custodian Guard (10 OC) and two 11-model Gretchin (22 OC) per Ork army, plus 6-model Warbikers/Deffkoptas. A Gretchin with 3 of 11 models on a contested objective keeps 16 OC out of range under REMAIN_STATIONARY. The corrected need (up to the deficit plus the COORD-5 cap of 14) then sends Warbikers, Deffkoptas or the Stompa to sit there, although a 3-4" Gretchin move would flip it. This is not worse than base, which flipped nothing, but it spends mobile damage units on objective duty.
issues.proposed_change: As a follow-up under a separate param: when a pass-1 holder on a non-held objective is not engaged and its in-range OC is below its unit OC, assign it a normal move toward the marker instead of a hold. Consume `unit_oc - in_range_oc` from the need, and keep `hold_adds_oc = 0` only when it stays stationary. Validate at s7454 as well: there Beta stepping in would cover the centre's need of 4 and could leave Gamma's lone flip in place, so this cannot replace the current change.

issues.situation: Evidence vs benchmark mismatch. Every cluster position, including s7454, comes from crucible_of_battle mission layouts with the sweep armies; none uses take_and_hold_mirror_1, the layout of all three benchmark fixtures. On the benchmark layout, about two-thirds of pass-1 fires (34 of 53 in the local logs) are centre holds in rounds 3-4 with "enemy can bring ~19-30 OC next move". About two-thirds of all 53 fires did not zero the need. There the patch mainly raises the need by the holder's unit OC, up to the COORD-5 projected cap (15 for Custodes, 14 for Orks), so pass 2 commits about one more 10-OC squad to the centre brawl than base. Past results argue this is not harmful: holding back lost 6.26 VP, and the reinforcement caps and the FIX_OVERCOMMIT veto did not help. Still, this, not the lone-flip mechanism, is what the benchmark will measure.
issues.proposed_change: Before shipping, replay one or two benchmark-layout positions, for example the V9 Custodes-mirror game at r3 P1 and r4 P1 (session_20261030_163127). Report benchmark results by fixture, with the round of first divergence. Keep the param so the change can be switched off per fixture if the Ork mirror diverges differently.

issues.situation: Phantom holders on non-benchmark layouts. `already_on_obj` ORs marker distance with the FIX-HELD-DUP area test, but `friendly_oc` uses only the area test. A unit 2-3.4" from a marker that sits outside its hosting areas therefore "holds" with 0 OC. Examples: Stormboyz 2.2" from the s7459 Ork-mirror centre marker, which sits in a 6.6" gap between the two areas; Tankbustas at s7408 obj_nml_1/2. Under the patch such a unit is re-pinned stationary every turn while another unit is sent. This cannot happen on take_and_hold_mirror_1 (each marker's 3.79" disc lies inside its area), but it affects sweeps and critic positions.
issues.proposed_change: In pass 1, treat a holder whose in-range OC at the objective is 0 as not on it (no hold candidate), so it gets a move candidate. Alternatively, make `already_on_obj` use only the area predicate when the objective has hosting areas.

reviews.fires_in_bench:
Likely to fire in a meaningful share of benchmark games, unlike V9's keeper fix (64/64 identical pairs).

**Custodes mirror (measured).** I counted pass-1 holds on non-held objectives (`assign_pass` hold, `oc_consumed > 0`, reason not "under threat"). This is exactly where [LONE_FLIP] fires. In about 420 pre-FIX_HELD_DUP full games on the benchmark layout (local session logs): 1.2% of round 2-5 movement phases, about 0.1 per game, with the need zeroed in only 0.3%. FIX_HELD_DUP (on in V9) roughly triples this: other-layout rollouts went from 4.1% to 11.6% of phases (zeroing from 1.6% to 7.0%). The only V9 benchmark-layout game in the logs fired in 2 of its 8 round 2-5 movement phases (3 holds, all zeroing, 2 of them keepers that had freed co-holders).

**Custodes mirror (estimate).** About 4-15% of round 2-5 movement phases, i.e. about 0.3-1 firing per game, in roughly a quarter to half of games. Most fires are P1/P2 centre holds in rounds 3-4 under heavy projected enemy OC. The plan changes in most fires, because the need rises even when base had not closed it.

**Orks mirror and Custodes vs Orks (estimate only).** There are no full-game logs. V9 sweep saves show the trigger configuration as often or more often than in the Custodes mirror (rounds 2-3: Orks mirror 4 of 15 saves, Custodes vs Orks 3 of 20, Custodes mirror 2 of 18). The benchmark Ork list has two 11-model Gretchin and 6-model bike/kopta units that often sit partly on the 7"x11.5" areas, so I expect a similar or higher rate. Many Ork units are engaged, however, and therefore excluded.

**Elsewhere.** It does not fire in round 1 normally. It does not fire at the brief's related s7455 r1 P2 Prosecutors position: the only holder there sits on P2's held home objective.
reviews.strengths:
**The root cause is real, and I verified it.** A pass-1 "hold" executes as REMAIN_STATIONARY (AIDecisionMaker.gd ~7031). For non-held states the need is `enemy - friendly + 1` (and COORD-5's projected need also subtracts friendly OC), so it already nets out the holder's in-range models. Base still subtracted the holder's whole unit OC, including models out of range. My static emulation of the s7454 save reproduces the designer's ledger: centre enemy_weak 5 vs 8, need 4. Friendly OC 5 is Beta's single model in range (3) plus a Blade Champion whose bodyguard is dead. That champion is not movable, because attached characters never get their own move. Beta's 9 OC zeroed the need, so the centre read as taken.

**The change is small and well contained.**
- It is a one-place ledger fix, gated by FIX_LONE_FLIP (0 restores base exactly), with no new score term or veto. That fits the lesson against broad trip or race vetoes.
- Held objectives are untouched, so KEEPER-PICK, KEEP-OC and KEEPER-RELEASE behave as before.
- Reserve placement reads `_initial_objective_oc_needs` directly and is unaffected.
- Pass-2 filters (LONE-TRIP, RACE-SKIP, TOO-LATE, DIM-RETURNS) still apply to the units the re-opened need attracts.

**The direction matches past benchmark evidence.** It puts more force on close contested objectives; holding back lost VP, and capping reinforcement did not help.

**Results so far are consistent.**
- At the finding: +29.2 over 6 seeds, all better.
- The 5 guardrails were reported unchanged. In my scan of 157 measured movement positions, the patch's trigger appears at only 11, all neutral except s7431 (unchanged per the designer) and one clear Ork-mirror position, s7408 r3 p2 (alternative +3.94), where the trigger is a phantom holder on a different objective. None of the measured harmful "go to the centre instead" positions (s7411, s7413, s7403, s7422) has the trigger.
- 19 related test suites pass.

**It is measurable.** It fires often enough in V9 for the benchmark to measure it.
reviews.summary:
Verdict ok. The design fixes a real double count: a stationary pass-1 holder on an objective we do not control had its whole unit OC subtracted from a need that already counted its in-range models. I traced the code path and reproduced the s7454 ledger (centre 5 vs 8, need 4, zeroed by Beta's 9 OC with only 3 in range).

Over full games the patch changes more than the lone-flip case:
- Every unit standing on a non-held objective now holds; base used to free co-holders once the keeper "covered" the need.
- On the benchmark layout, which has large hosting areas and 5-model Custodian Guard and 11-model Gretchin, the typical fire is a round 3-4 centre hold under heavy projected enemy OC. There the patch commits about one more squad to the centre.
- A holder later converted to an attack re-opens the need on top of an unreduced need.

None of these has a demonstrated cost. Pinning only differs from base in close fights, and extra reinforcement has not hurt in past benchmarks. The attack-conversion overcount is rare in V9 logs. So all issues are minor, each with a concrete refinement: a consistent co-holder exit, re-opening only the in-range OC, moving partial holders onto the objective, skipping phantom holders, and replaying benchmark-layout positions before shipping.

Estimated firing in the benchmark: about 0.3-1 movement phases per Custodes-mirror game under V9, roughly 3x the pre-FIX_HELD_DUP rate, in a quarter to half of games; similar or higher in the Ork fixtures (not measured). The benchmark should therefore see real divergence. Files: /home/user/warhammer-40k-godot/tools/ai_lab/r4_designs/lone_flip/root.patch and root.json. My emulator and scan scripts are in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-warhammer-40k-godot/72451711-ff9e-5f4b-a27c-d739a3534701/scratchpad/tools/ (emu.py, trig_scan.py, sess_scan.py).

issues.situation: The fix breaks the COORD-4 attack-conversion re-open (pass 2.5, base AIDecisionMaker.gd lines 10449-10457). Path: a melee-seeker holds an objective we do not control in pass 1, for example a recon_stomps Stormboyz unit or a standalone Blade Champion whose bodyguard died (Custodian Guard and Boyz are not seekers). With FIX_LONE_FLIP on, the hold sets oc_consumed to 0 and the need stays at need0. Pass 2 then sends other units to fill need0. Next, _melee_chase_gate turns the holder into an ATTACK. This is the usual outcome for a partial holder: its centroid is off the marker, so the 'stays on contested objective' exemption does not apply, and an enemy is almost always inside the 10-18" hold limit. The re-open still computes reopened = max(oc_consumed, h_threat - (friendly_oc - unit_oc) + 1), which is about need0 + unit_oc, and adds it to the ledger. That formula assumes the hold had already consumed the need. So need0, which pass 2 already filled, is asked for a second time. The COORD-4 backfill, including OBJ-BACKFILL-1 switches that pull units off other captures, then sends about need0 more OC than base would, on top of base's existing (unit_oc - in-range) slack. Example: at s7438 r3 P2 (Orks), the centre has Lootas and Stormboyz partial holders and a static need near 15. Pass 2 fills the 15, then the Stormboyz conversion re-opens 13 or more. That is about 28 OC planned for the centre against about 13 on base. The fix's own test never puts a seeker on the objective, so it does not cover this path.
issues.proposed_change: Mark LONE_FLIP holds in pass 1, for example assignments[uid]["lone_flip_hold"] = true when hold_adds_oc is set to 0. In pass 2.5, when such a hold turns into an ATTACK, re-open only the OC that leaves with it: its OC in range, from _unit_oc_at_position(h_eval.position, uid, a_unit, friendly_units, hd_obj_by_id.get(a_oid, {}), hd_mm). Use unit_oc as a conservative fallback. Do not use h_threat - h_left + 1. Gate this on the same param so that 0 still gives base. Add a test: a melee-only holder with one model on an enemy-held objective, an enemy within 10", and a second unit that pass 2 sends there. Assert that the objective's re-opened need equals the holder's OC in range, not need0 + unit_oc.

issues.situation: test_held_objective_ledger_unchanged only asserts that the sole holder holds. This passes on base. It would also pass if the held_safe/held_threatened exclusion were deleted, because a sole holder always holds as keeper or because remaining > 0. So nothing pins the exclusion that keeps the KEEP-OC and keeper ledger unchanged.
issues.proposed_change: Build a held_threatened objective with a COORD-5 projected need, for example an enemy squad one move away. Assert that the holder's oc_consumed equals min(unit_oc, need) and that the remaining need is the base value. Optionally, assert that a second movable holder on that objective is still freed as on base.

issues.situation: The test's _plan helper calls _evaluate_all_objectives(..., 2) and _assign_units_to_objectives(..., 2, 2) with battle_round 2, while the snapshot's meta says round 3. Round-dependent terms (urgency, denial, stay bonus) see round 2, but _melee_chase_gate and the hold logic read round 3 from the snapshot.
issues.proposed_change: Pass 3, matching the snapshot, or read the round from snap.meta.battle_round.

issues.situation: The partial holder still makes a REMAIN_STATIONARY hold with 2 of its 3 models off the area. At s7454 r3, Beta moving its two other models onto the centre area would add 6 OC: 11 vs 8 flips the centre without pulling Alpha off obj_home_2. The fix corrects the ledger, but another unit now does what the holder could do itself. The report's risk (2) says this, and it is not a bug.
issues.proposed_change: Leave this out of this patch. As a follow-up, let a partial holder on an objective we do not control take a 'move' onto its own objective when its out-of-range models would close the gap, and measure that separately.

issues.situation: Gaps in the report. (a) The fire counts come only from Custodes-mirror replays, but 2 of the 3 benchmark fixtures involve Orks. There, COORD-5 projected needs left open by the fix are large (for example need about 15, which means two extra units at s7438), and Stormboyz reach the COORD-4 path above. The 'Assigned ... to HOLD (OC: %d ...)' line also still prints the full unit OC, although that OC no longer fills anything.
issues.proposed_change: Reword to 'need stays %d (base would set %d)'. The existing HOLD print can stay as it is, since no debug log should be removed.

reviews.fires_in_bench: It fires often, from round 2 onward, so it will not give the 64/64 identical pairs of V9's keeper fix. The trigger is any plan build where a movable, non-engaged unit has at least one model on the hosting area of an objective we do not control (enemy_weak, enemy_strong, contested or uncontrolled). On Crucible of Battle terrain objectives (7"x11.5" areas, a 16"-tall centre pair; the same as the 3 fixtures), partial holders are common. I checked this statically, without running Godot, on 190 saved movement positions from the sweeps (Custodes, Orks and Space Wolves; rounds 1-3). The trigger appears in 0/99 round-1 positions, 3-6/45 round-2 positions and 8-11/46 round-3 positions. The lower bounds exclude units that had already moved at the save. In 3-7 of these, mostly round 3, base's hold had cut the need to 0, so a plan change is near-certain. Rounds 4-5 are not sampled and are usually more contested. My estimate is about 1-2 fires per game for the candidate seat, and at least one changed plan in roughly 40-60% of games, first diverging in round 2-3. The effect is probably larger in the two Orks fixtures, where re-opened COORD-5 projected needs are big and Stormboyz holders also reach the COORD-4 double count. The designer's own one-round replays agree: 5 [LONE_FLIP] lines in 6 Custodes-mirror replays, 2 of which changed decisions.
reviews.strengths: The root cause is real and correctly identified. The need (enemy_oc - friendly_oc + 1, and COORD-5's projected need) already nets out every friendly model in range, and HOLD runs as REMAIN_STATIONARY, so taking away the holder's whole unit OC double-counts its in-range models and credits OC from models that never arrive. My static rebuild of s7454 r3 P2 gives exactly the report's numbers: obj_center enemy_weak 5 vs 8, need 4; Beta has 1 of 3 models on the area, unit OC 9, so base sets need to 0. The change is about 10 lines in one place, with no score term or veto, so it is not a broad trip or race veto like FIX_FAR_TRIP. FIX_LONE_FLIP=0 gives the same decisions as base (the only extra is a parameters_used entry). Held objectives are untouched. It adds a [LONE_FLIP] log, removes no log, and costs almost nothing. The patch applies cleanly to 5e70bc2. The test calls _evaluate_all_objectives and _assign_units_to_objectives like the other FIX tests, pins the param and erases it afterwards, and fails on base for the right reason (oc_consumed 7 instead of 0; the runner goes to obj_side). It also has a param-0 test. The guardrail claims match my static check: no movable holder on an objective we do not control at g1, g4, g5 or s7452; at g3 the centre holder had already moved; at g2 it fires on obj_home_2 only.
reviews.summary: This is a sound root-cause fix. The pass-1 need-ledger double count is real, and the fix corrects it with a minimal, param-gated change that should fire in a large share of benchmark games, so the benchmark can measure it. It has one real bug: holds on objectives we do not control now leave the need open, but pass 2.5's COORD-4 re-open still adds the full need-without-holder, as if the hold had covered it. A melee-seeker holder that turns into an ATTACK (Stormboyz, a standalone Blade Champion) therefore asks for about need0 extra OC on top of what pass 2 already sent, and the backfill over-commits. The fix is small: flag LONE_FLIP holds and re-open only the holder's in-range OC, with a test. Also tighten the weak held-state test, fix the test's round argument, and add Orks-fixture fire counts. After that it is ready for the benchmark. The full-game risk of more units converging on contested objectives is still unmeasured.

issues.situation: The patch does not execute the move the evidence measured. The redirect keeps the planner's mode, which at the finding (s7454 r3 P2) is a Normal move: Gamma's gap to the centre is 11.2", more than M+2". For a Normal move, the executor (AIDecisionMaker.gd ~L7328-7345 at 5e70bc2) aims 70% at the unit's phase-plan charge target and 30% at the objective whenever the target is within M+12". `_build_phase_plan` picks that charge target without looking at the movement plan, and scores enemies on objectives x1.3. In the original game Gamma's move read 'moving toward charge target Custodian Guard Sodality Gamma', which is P1's holder of obj_nml_1, 13.9" away. After the redirect, the aim point is 0.7 x that holder + 0.3 x the centre. My straight-line estimate puts Gamma about 14.2" from obj_center and 7.5" from the same holder; the base move ends about 3.9" from obj_nml_1 and 5.9" from the holder. So the redirected unit neither joins the centre fight this turn nor keeps its charge approach. The +21.5 VP evidence is for an Advance straight to the centre (the Advance branch has no blend). The design's own measurement of its Normal move is +11.33 [-0.70, 23.37] over only 6 seeds. In V9-era logs, 976 of 1161 Normal-move flips carried a charge intent, so most Normal-move redirects will be pulled back the same way.
issues.proposed_change: When LONE_FLIP fires: (a) erase the unit's charge intent (`_phase_plan[player].charge_intent[uid]`), retarget it to an enemy within about 6" of the new objective, or set an assignment flag the T7-23 blend checks so it skips the blend. (b) Use Advance when the live fight is out of Normal-move reach this turn but within M+2" plus control range and we are behind there now (enemy_weak): that is the measured +21.5 move. (c) Re-measure with FIX_LONE_FLIP=1 end-to-end (no ROLLOUT override) at s7454 r3 over 24-36 seeds before shipping.

issues.situation: The 'live fight' test is broader than the evidence. held_threatened only means our OC is higher and any enemy unit's centroid is within 12". For that state, `friendly_oc + unit_oc > enemy_oc` is always true. Projected enemy OC is ignored, and so is the OC the plan already sends to that objective. Against an enemy_strong flip the base weights already give -5 vs +6.4, plus 1.5-3.75 for holding under threat, so the 10-point margin is met almost automatically. In practice, a unit walking toward an enemy-held objective is pulled back to stack on one we already hold. That is the FAR_TRIP failure mode (units taken off pressure; -6.26 VP/game in the Custodes mirror). Measured example, s7438 r2 P1 (Custodes vs Orks): Custodian Guard Beta's lone flip of the enemy home (0 v 20). The redirect target would be the centre, which we hold 8 v 5 with about 1 enemy OC one move away. That exact move measured E -1.92 [-8.62, 4.78]. s7436 r2 P2 (home held 11 v 4, 5 projected) is another surplus target. 2 of the 7 measured flip positions that meet the trigger's state conditions are surplus holds.
issues.proposed_change: Accept an alternative only while it has a real shortfall: friendly_oc + incoming + OC of units the plan already sends there <= enemy_oc + projected_enemy_oc. Stop once it is covered, and count already-assigned movers in the 'friendly + this unit > enemy' test too. This keeps the finding (5 v 8, 2 projected) and drops surplus holds. It effectively aims the redirect at the pass-1 double count, which is the cause the evidence supports.

issues.situation: `ours` only counts units assigned earlier in the single greedy pass 2. The plan is built once per phase in score order, so when the first unit of a multi-unit flip is checked, the units the plan would send after it are invisible, and ours is just its own OC. In V9-era session logs (1709 movement phases), 318 of 672 flips whose first unit alone was below the enemy OC were coordinated flips: 2 or more units whose total reached the enemy OC. If that first unit has a live-fight alternative it is redirected. The second unit then either goes alone (e.g. 9 v 15, the very pattern this fix exists to stop) or is redirected too, and a winnable flip is abandoned. The report's guardrail reasons ('Beta is also sent, plan OC 18 > 11 / 18 > 15') do not match the code. At s7458 r1 ('needs 3 more OC after this unit' shows Alpha was assigned first) and at s7457 r3 (Beta's candidate is checked first), the checked unit reads LONE (9 v 11, 9 v 15). Those guardrails stayed unchanged only because no live fight was within 2 moves.
issues.proposed_change: Run LONE-FLIP as a post-pass after the pass-2 loop (before KEEPER-RELEASE). For each enemy-held objective, sum friendly + incoming + every unit the final plan sends there. Redirect only when that total is below enemy_oc, restoring the flip objective's need from each moved unit's oc_consumed. Alternatively, in-loop, count still-unassigned units' RACE-ARMY friendly_arrivals within LONE_FLIP_MAX_TURNS as joiners, as lone_trip_oc's army term does.

issues.situation: A measured-harmful position with the same shape was not checked. s7411 r3 P1 (Custodes mirror, s1b case): Custodian Guard Beta's lone flip of obj_nml_2 (26 enemy OC in range) while the centre was 11 v 14 with Custodian Guard Alpha on it. Moving Beta to the centre, which is exactly the redirect's target, measured harmful: E -2.25 [-4.26, -0.24] over 12 seeds. With the finding (+21.5) and s7438 (-1.92), the evidence for the general rule is one strong positive and mixed others.
issues.proposed_change: Add s7411 r3 P1 and s7438 r2 P1 to the guardrail replays, from the phase-start plan, with the fix on. Treat a non-positive result there as a reason to narrow the trigger per the shortfall rule above.

issues.situation: Report accuracy. For s7455 r2 P1 the report says 'obj_center is uncontrolled'. At that save, Custodian Guard Alpha and Blade Champion Beta (already moved this phase) stand in the centre's terrain area: 8 v 14, a live fight by the design's own test. It stayed unchanged for another reason, probably the 10-point margin between two 2-turn enemy_weak options. The guardrail table reads the original decision text rather than the replanned state.
issues.proposed_change: Re-derive each guardrail verdict from the replay's own [LONE_FLIP] and plan log lines at the save state, and record why the redirect did not fire (no live fight / margin / not lone).

issues.situation: Scope and consistency. The pass-1 double count stays: in V9-era logs a pass-1 HOLD consumed need in 235 of 1709 movement phases, and the redirect only covers the subset whose fallback is a lone flip. The COORD-4 backfill and the KEEPER-RELEASE application call apply_capture_assignment without LONE-FLIP, so both can still create lone flips. LONE_FLIP_MAX_TURNS is read as a constant, not through get_param, so profiles cannot tune it.
issues.proposed_change: Apply the same check in the backfill and keeper-release paths, read LONE_FLIP_MAX_TURNS through get_param, and note the remaining double count as a known limit (or correct pass 1 to subtract only the OC a holder adds beyond friendly_oc).

issues.situation: Full-game costs a one-round rollout only partly sees. Planner points measure the 10-point margin, and the flip's threat_delta (-16 at the finding) often supplies most of it; that is a survival heuristic, not VP. Redirects driven by threat give up kills on the flip objective's holders (P2's Purge-the-Foe pays destroyed_min every turn) and quarter or enemy-zone presence (the finding's base branch scored Engage on All Fronts +3). An uncontested enemy objective also lets the enemy's KEEP-OC free its holders to join the centre next turn.
issues.proposed_change: Compute the margin without the flip's threat_delta and overwatch terms, or require that the alternative's VP value exceeds the flip's VP (including secondary-card terms). Check full-game secondary VP separately in the benchmark report.

reviews.fires_in_bench: Rough estimate, not replayed (repository is read-only for this review): about 0.4-0.6 redirects per game in the Custodes mirror, about 0.6-2 in the Orks mirror, and about 0.5-1 in Custodes vs Orks. It is rare in round 1 (it needs our models already in a fight) and in round 5 (lone flips are rare and the 2-move target is too late). Basis: in V9-era session logs (1709 movement phases), flips where the unit's own OC is below the enemy OC run 0.52 / 0.73 / 0.45 per player-phase for Custodes in rounds 2/3/4, and about 1.3-2.6 for Orks. I rebuilt the saved positions of the 47 measured flips: 7 meet the redirect's state conditions (lone, plus a live fight within 2 moves). Four of those are enemy_strong flips, where the 10-point margin is near certain (-5 vs +6.4 base weights). So roughly 10-15% of lone flips fire. That means roughly a third to two-thirds of benchmark games should diverge from base, so it will register (unlike V9's keeper fix with 64/64 identical pairs). About half the 'lone' readings come from coordinated flips (issue 3), and a share of firings land on surplus holds (issue 2). Fixing those would cut the rate, maybe toward 0.2-0.4 per game. The designer's own count (1 change in 6 one-round replays) fits about 0.5 per Custodes game.
reviews.strengths: The double count it starts from is real. Pass 1 subtracts the holder's whole unit_oc although friendly_oc already counts its models in range, and in the logs this zeroes a live objective's need in about 14% of movement phases. The design is gated on FIX_LONE_FLIP, and 0 gives exactly base behaviour (the closure returns {} first). It is a redirect, not a veto: the unit always gets an order. It fires only when the flip loses against the enemy OC standing there now, and it re-applies TOO-LATE / RACE-SKIP / LONE-TRIP to the target. At the finding it picks the measured target and direction (Gamma to obj_center). The narration ([LONE_FLIP] log and coordination_note) is clear. The tests cover the redirect, a winnable flip kept, no live fight kept, and the param off.
reviews.summary:
Verdict: revise. The redirect starts from a real, common accounting bug, but over full games it is likely to misfire, for three concrete reasons.
(1) The patch does not execute the move that was measured. The redirect keeps a Normal move, and the executor aims that move 70% at the unit's charge target, which is set independently of the plan (at the finding, the obj_nml_1 holder). The redirected Gamma therefore ends about 14" from the centre and 7.5" from its target. The +21.5 VP is for an Advance straight to the centre; the patch's own move measured +11.3 [-0.7, 23.4] over 6 seeds.
(2) The 'live fight' test accepts surplus holds (any enemy within 12" of an objective we hold) and ignores OC the plan already sends there. Against enemy_strong flips the 10-point margin is almost automatic, so units are pulled back to stack on held ground: the FAR_TRIP failure mode. At s7438 that move measured -1.92.
(3) `ours` only sees units assigned earlier in the greedy pass, so the first unit of a coordinated flip reads as lone. That is 47% of such flips in the logs, and the report's guardrail reasons for s7458 r1 and s7457 r3 are wrong on this point.
s7411 r3 P1, which the designer did not check, has the same shape and measured harmful (-2.25 [-4.26, -0.24]).
Fixes: drop or retarget the charge intent and use Advance on redirect; require a real shortfall at the target (ours + planned <= enemy + projected); run the check as a post-pass over the final plan; re-measure with the fix on (no override) over 24-36 seeds.

My read-only analysis scripts are in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-warhammer-40k-godot/72451711-ff9e-5f4b-a27c-d739a3534701/scratchpad/tools/ (objstate.py, flipscan.py, altcheck.py).

issues.situation: The test for a 'lone' flip depends on greedy order. lone_flip_redirect builds `ours` from friendly OC in range, units en route, c's OC and only the units already in `assignments` for c's objective. Pass 2 is greedy, so the first unit of a joint flip is always checked alone. Example (Custodes mirror): the enemy holds X with OC 14, and Gamma and Alpha (OC 9 each) are the plan's flippers. In base, Gamma takes the need from 15 to 6 and Alpha from 6 to 0, so 18 beats 14. Beta stands partly on the centre, so the centre's need reads 0. With the fix, Gamma is processed first, sees 9 < 14 and is redirected to the centre. Alpha is then checked alone (9 < 14). If Alpha has no live fight within 2 turns, it goes to X alone: the fix creates the very lone flip it is meant to stop. This is close in real positions. At s7458 r1, Alpha was assigned FIRST (its card says 'needs 3 more OC after this unit': need 12 -> 3), so its check saw 9 < 11. It kept the flip only because P1 has no live fight in round 1. At s7455 r2, the first nml_1 flipper saw 9 < 11, and the centre (P1 8 vs P2 14 in range, enemy_weak, 8+9 > 14, 2 turns) passed every filter except the +10 score margin. The report's guardrail reasons for s7458 r1 and s7457 r3 ('Beta is also sent, plan OC 18 > 11/15, so the flip is not lone') describe behaviour the code does not have.
issues.proposed_change: Before redirecting, add the OC of units that can still join. For example: `var could := ours; for j in candidates: if j.objective_id == c.objective_id and j.unit_id != c.unit_id and not assigned_unit_ids.has(j.unit_id) and j.action in ["move","advance"] and int(j.turns_to_reach) <= maxi(int(c.turns_to_reach), 2) and not too_late.call(j) and not race_hopeless.call(j) and not lone_trip.call(j): could += int(j.unit_oc)`. Return {} when `could >= enemy_oc`, or reuse the RACE-ARMY 'army' figure from lone_trip_oc. Another option: run LONE-FLIP as a post-pass after pass 2 (like KEEPER_RELEASE), when every unit sent to the flip is known, and give back the redirected unit's oc_consumed. Add a unit test: two OC-9 flippers vs 14 enemy OC, where the first-processed one has a live-fight alternative; both must still go to the flip.

issues.situation: The target filter accepts any held_threatened objective. There we already out-OC the enemy, so 'friendly_oc + unit_oc > enemy_oc' is always true. It also ignores units the plan has already sent there. So a lone flipper can be sent to stack on an objective it cannot change, e.g. ours 13 vs theirs 0 with one enemy unit within 12". That is close to round 2's 'units held back' pattern. The measured finding is a fight we were losing (5 vs 8), not this case. In my offline scan of saved V9 positions, 11 of the 15 precondition hits outside the finding use this held_threatened branch (Ork fixtures: Battlewagons and Lootas next to objectives held 13-26 OC to 0-4). So it may be the main way the fix fires in the bench, and no guardrail or rollout covers it.
issues.proposed_change: Accept a target only when this unit changes control. Set fo = friendly_oc + OC of units already assigned there with move/advance, and threat = enemy_oc + projected_enemy_oc. Require `fo <= threat and fo + alt.unit_oc > enemy_oc`. This keeps contested/enemy_weak fights we are behind in, and held_threatened only when it is really at risk next move. Or drop held_threatened from the state list until a rollout measures it.

issues.situation: Several of the report's guardrail reasons do not match the saved positions or the code. s7455 r2 P1: obj_center is NOT uncontrolled. At that decision, P1 has OC 8 in range (Guard Alpha with 2 of 3 models in range, plus Blade Champion Beta; both already moved) vs P2 OC 14. That is enemy_weak with friendly_oc > 0, 8+9 > 14, and 2 turns away for Beta and Gamma: a live fight by the design's own test. Only the +10 margin (or the processing order) keeps the flip. s7458 r1 and s7457 r3 are unchanged because no live fight lies within 2 turns (P1 in round 1; in s7457, nml_1 is 3 turns away and the centre and home_1 are held_safe), not because the flip is joint. s7452 r2, which the brief lists, is missing from the report. reviews.fires_in_bench: Rare, but not zero. It can fire only at plan time, once per movement phase. It needs (a) a pass-2 capture of an enemy-held objective that the units assigned so far cannot out-OC now, and (b) for the same unit, a covered objective (need 0) in state contested, enemy_weak or held_threatened, with our models on it, within 2 turns, scoring at least +10 more. Of the 8 V9 Custodes-mirror flip decisions in measured_positions.json, only the finding (s7454 r3) meets every condition. s7455 r2 meets all except, apparently, the +10 margin. The others fail: s7451 r1 and s7458 r1 (round 1, no live fight), s7457 r3 (live fight 3 turns away), s7452 r2, s7455 r3 and s7456 r3 (not lone, or the only target is a hold). I also approximated the planner offline over the 108 saved V9 movement positions from the 24 round-4 sweep games (lfg_review/trigger_scan.py). The conditions other than the score margin hold in 2 of 35 Custodes-mirror positions (one is the finding), 5 of 34 Custodes-vs-Orks positions and 9 of 39 Orks-mirror positions. Most Ork hits come from Battlewagons and Lootas next to held_threatened objectives with a large surplus, and several of those units actually made support moves or were at reserve-arrival steps. So real fires are fewer than the hits. Estimate: about 0.1-0.4 fires per Custodes-mirror game, in rounds 2-4 (never in P1's round 1), and similar or slightly more in the two Ork fixtures through the held_threatened branch. Only the candidate seat can fire, so I expect roughly 10-30% of bench pairs to differ, each by one unit's move in one phase: enough to avoid V9's all-identical pairs, but any gain will be small against bench noise. The double count itself (a losing objective's need zeroed by a pass-1 hold) appears in 1 of 35, 2 of 39 and 2 of 34 of those positions.
reviews.strengths: The change is narrow and fully gated. lone_flip_redirect returns {} first thing when FIX_LONE_FLIP < 0.5, and the call site acts only on a non-empty result, so param 0 gives the base behaviour exactly (only parameters_used gains two reads). It is not a veto: it never holds a unit back. It only moves the unit to an objective where our models already fight, which respects the round-2 FAR_TRIP lesson. It re-checks TOO-LATE, RACE-SKIP and LONE-TRIP on the target. DIM-RETURNS cannot skip these states, and FAR_TRIP/OVERCOMMIT are off. Empty evaluations are guarded, ids are consistent (alt.unit_id == uid, so the note lands on the right unit), and the cost is negligible: early exits, a sorted break, and at most one call per pass-2 candidate. It adds a [LONE_FLIP] print and a coordination_note that thinking_steps carry into game records, and it removes no logs. The test drives the real planner, pins and erases the override, and fails on base for the right reason. My OC probe of the s7454 r3 save reproduces the report's numbers (centre: ours 5 vs theirs 8, with 1 of Beta's 3 models in range; obj_nml_1: theirs 14). Read through the code, the decision check (Gamma goes to obj_center, Normal move) matches what the patch would do. The report is candid that the root double count is left in place.
reviews.summary: The design adds a redirect in pass 2. When a capture cannot out-OC the enemy standing on the objective now, the unit instead goes to an objective within 2 turns that scores at least 10 more and where our models already fight. This fixes the finding (Gamma goes to obj_center) but leaves the root cause alone. That root cause is a real double count: the need is computed net of friendly_oc, and then pass 1 subtracts the holder's whole OC again. In the finding, the centre's need of 4 was zeroed by Beta's 9 OC, although only 3 of it was in range and Beta remains stationary. Gating, null safety, ids, cost and logging are sound. The major problem is that the 'lone' check depends on greedy order: it counts only units assigned earlier. So it can split a joint flip the plan would win and leave the second unit to flip alone. The report's s7458 r1 and s7457 r3 reasoning assumes the opposite, and s7455 r2 is one score margin away from showing it. The held_threatened branch also widens the trigger beyond the measured case, and it probably accounts for most fires in the Ork fixtures. Verdict: revise. Count the units that can still join (or move the check to a post-pass). Restrict targets to fights the unit actually tips. Add a joint-flip test. Correct the guardrail reasons and add s7452 r2. Measure the Normal-move action with more seeds. I did not run Godot (read-only review), so the test results and replay fire counts are the designer's claims; my code reading supports them. My analysis scripts are /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-warhammer-40k-godot/72451711-ff9e-5f4b-a27c-d739a3534701/scratchpad/lfg_review/oc_probe.py, /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-warhammer-40k-godot/72451711-ff9e-5f4b-a27c-d739a3534701/scratchpad/lfg_review/trigger_scan.py and /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-warhammer-40k-godot/72451711-ff9e-5f4b-a27c-d739a3534701/scratchpad/lfg_review/dc_scan.py.

HOLD runs as REMAIN_STATIONARY (base ~L7031), so the double count it removes is real. At s7454 it makes the same plan as narrow: Alpha takes the centre with a Normal move and Gamma goes to home_2. That is not the measured unit or mode. Over 6 seeds with the fix in both seats the mean went from -30.3 to -1.2, better on every seed. My static check found no measured-harmful guardrail moving: at s7455 r3 obj_nml_2 is held 17 v 0; at s7452 r2 the centre is held 3 v 0; s7455 r2, s7457 and s7458 have no movable holder on a non-held objective. Of 13 measured movement positions with its trigger, the only harmful one is s7431, where the current base already plays the centre move. The test asserts oc_consumed == 0 and fails on base (7); it does not depend on pass-3 screening. MAJOR: pass 2.5's COORD-4 re-open still adds max(oc_consumed, threat-(F-U)+1) on top of a need that pass 2 already filled. This path is common in the bench because the fixture Custodian Guard (ranged spear S4 A2) and the Blade Champions are melee seekers, unlike the sweep's Sodality lists. On the benchmark layout it behaves the same as root. verdict.reasons:
The double count is real, and I checked it in the code. For every non-held state, the need is enemy_oc - friendly_oc + 1, and COORD-5's projected need also nets out friendly_oc. friendly_oc already includes the holder's models in range, and a pass-1 HOLD executes as REMAIN_STATIONARY. Even so, pass 1 subtracted the holder's whole unit OC. At s7454 I rebuilt the position statically. The centre is enemy 5 v 8 (Beta has 1 of 3 models in range, OC 3, plus a lone Blade Champion with OC 2), so the need is 4. Beta's OC 9 zeroed it.

Narrow and root fix the cause with the same one-place, param-gated ledger change, and FIX_LONE_FLIP=0 restores base exactly. They add no veto or score term, so they respect the round-2/round-3 lessons, and they push force toward contested primary objectives. They do not hold units back.

A static scan of all measured movement positions found the trigger at 13. Only s7454 and s7408 are clear, and s7408 is a phantom that only root acts on. The one harmful position, s7431, is unchanged from the current base, and no measured-harmful alternative is moved toward.

On the benchmark layout these designs will fire. Hosting areas are 7"x11.5", and the centre spans 11.6"x10". Reviewers estimate about 0.3-2 fires per seat per game from round 2, mostly at the centre in rounds 3-5. A large share of side-swapped pairs should therefore diverge, unlike V9's 64/64 identical pairs.

Root beats narrow on four points:
- Its rule is the principled one: every state the ledger computes net of friendly OC, including uncontrolled, where a holder's in-range OC is 0 by definition.
- Its test pins oc_consumed == 0 directly and does not depend on pass-3 screening.
- It does not print spurious fire lines when the need is already 0.
- It applies to V9R without fuzz.

Both share one real defect, which the two code reviews flag as major and which I confirmed. Pass 2.5's COORD-4 re-open assumes the hold consumed the need. When a zero-consumption holder converts to ATTACK, it adds the full no-holder shortfall on top of a need that pass 2 already filled. With the finding's numbers that is 4 + 13 = 17, when the true need is 7. In the bench this path is common: the fixture Custodian Guard (5 x OC2, ranged spear S4 A2) and Blade Champions are melee seekers, and Custodes aggression of 1.5 gives a 12-14" hold-leave limit. So the change is required.

Game ranks last. It patches one consequence and leaves the cause. It executes a different move than the one measured, its 'lone' test depends on greedy order, its target filter admits surplus stacks, and it fires rarely.

None of the three reaches the newly confirmed s7455 r2 P1 finding (+5.92, a score-driven lone flip with no movable holder) or s7455 r1 (round 1, no holder). Both are out of scope for this mechanism.
required_changes: Pass 1 (root's LONE-FLIP branch): when hold_adds_oc is set to 0, also set assignments[uid]["lone_flip_hold"] = true. This lets later passes tell zero-consumption holds from base holds.

PASS 2.5 (COORD-4 attack conversion, base ~L10449-10457): applies when a converted assignment has action 'hold', lone_flip_hold set, and FIX_LONE_FLIP >= 0.5. In that case set reopened = _unit_oc_at_position(a.get("objective_pos", Vector2.INF), uid, a_unit, snapshot.get("units", {}), hd_obj_by_id.get(a_oid, {}), hd_mm). This is the in-range OC that actually leaves, and it is 0 for a battle-shocked or phantom holder. Use it instead of maxi(oc_consumed, h_threat - h_left + 1). Keep the existing formula for all other holds and whenever the param is 0, so that param 0 still reproduces V9R exactly. Keep the [COORD-4] log line.

Add a unit test for that path in test_ai_fix_lone_flip.gd. Setup: a melee-seeker partial holder with the fixture Custodian Guard profile (ranged spear S4 A2 AP-1 D2, melee S7 A5 AP-2 D2). One model is on an enemy-held objective, its centroid is more than 3.79" from the marker, and an enemy is within the hold-leave limit. Add a runner whose OC exactly fills the need, and 2-3 spare units. Assert three things: the holder becomes ATTACK, its oc_consumed is 0, and the COORD-4 backfill sends at most the one unit needed to replace the holder's in-range OC. The unpatched re-open (about threat-(F-U)+1 on top of the filled need) sends more. The test must fail with the pass-2.5 change removed and pass with it.
grafts: From narrow: read FIX_LONE_FLIP once before the pass-1 loop (var lone_flip_on) and reuse it in pass 2.5. Also adopt its clearer log wording ('holds but adds no OC (already counted: friendly X vs enemy Y) — need stays N'). Change root's '(was %d -> %d)' to '(base would set %d)'.

Tests, from both code reviews: make the held-state case meaningful by putting an enemy one move away, so the held_threatened projected need is > 0, then assert oc_consumed == min(unit_oc, need) and that the free unit is not sent. Add a contested (tie) case where a free unit is sent. Add a two-co-holder enemy-held case asserting that both hold with oc_consumed 0. Pass battle round 3 to match the snapshot meta.

In the [LONE_FLIP] line, print how many co-holders the objective keeps. Benchmark diffs can then be attributed to the re-opened need or to co-holder pinning; the latter is a behaviour change that neither design tests.

Follow-ups, each under its own param with its own value check, not in this patch: (a) a partial holder on a non-held objective moves its out-of-range models onto it instead of REMAIN_STATIONARY, consuming unit_oc minus its in-range OC (at s7454 Beta could cover the centre itself; the bench's 11-model Gretchin with 1 model in range stays pinned today); (b) a non-keeper co-holder may leave when its best other candidate outscores the hold, adding its in-range OC back to the need; (c) a holder with 0 in-range OC (phantom) is not treated as on the objective.

From game: its idea, sending a lone flip that cannot win to a fight where our models already stand, is the mechanism behind the newly confirmed s7455 r2 P1 finding (+5.92), which root cannot reach. Treat it as a separate design and take it up only with the reviewers' fixes: run it as a post-pass over the final plan, require a real shortfall at the target, drop held_threatened surplus targets, and handle charge intent and Advance. First check s7411 r3 P1 (-2.25, harmful) and s7438 r2 P1 (-1.92).

If the Ork fixtures show over-commitment into fights the planner rates as lost, keep base consumption on enemy_strong and apply zero consumption only to enemy_weak, contested and uncontrolled (narrow game review, issue 3).

Check the [LONE_FLIP] lines, check that the [COORD-4] re-open after an attack conversion equals the holder's in-range OC, count the co-holders pinned, and confirm that the backfill and OBJ-BACKFILL-1 pull no extra units.

verdict.merge_risk:
Medium. The code change is about 10 lines in one place in pass 1, and it applies to V9R with an offset only (I dry-ran it). It still changes the need ledger for every pass-1 hold on an objective we do not control. That happens in a large share of benchmark games: an estimated 0.3-2 fires per seat per game from round 2, mostly the centre in rounds 3-5, in all three fixtures. It also pins every co-holder on such objectives in place; base freed them, and nothing has measured that.

Until the required pass-2.5 change lands, every melee-seeker holder that converts to ATTACK over-asks the backfill by about the whole need. In the fixtures those seekers are Custodian Guard, Blade Champions and Ork melee units, so the plan systematically over-commits to contested objectives.

The evidence of value is thin. It comes from one position (s7454), 6 seeds with the fix in both seats, and a different unit and mode than the measured alternative. The second confirmed finding (s7455 r2 P1, +5.92) and s7455 r1 are not addressed. The full-game effect on secondary VP is unknown, and the benchmark has to decide it. Param 0 restores base exactly, so rollback is trivial.
